minor.title: The orphan-rev gate's 'full 40-hex sha' rule is untested at its length boundary: a 39-hex rev passes as pinned (mutant X1 survives, non-equivalent)
minor.detail: FULL_SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/ (check-patch-rev.ts:35) is exercised by rev-short.toml (7 hex), rev-uppercase.toml (40 upper) and the accepted 40-hex fixtures only. With `{39,40}` the 20 tests stay green; a 39-hex rev is a valid abbreviation for git, cargo (`rev` accepts any revision) and the GitHub compare endpoint, so the mutant's behaviour is observable: the entry is printed as 'pinned by a full sha' and the network check runs on it. ADR-0031 D2 and I-28 say 'SHA complet'. One fixture (`rev-39hex.toml`, and symmetrically a 41-character string) closes it. Impact is small in practice (39-hex prefixes are unique), the point is the specification's boundary, the same class as round 2's silent forms.
